summary: Enrique Adolfo Jimenez Airport (ONX) is a medium-sized airport serving Colón, Panama, the country's second-largest city located on the Caribbean coast near the Atlantic entrance to the Panama Canal. Named after Enrique Adolfo Jiménez, a former President of Panama (1945–1948), the airport primarily handles domestic and regional flights, supporting both tourism and commerce tied to the Colón Free Zone, one of the world's largest re-export hubs.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate from Enrique Adolfo Jimenez Airport?
A: The airport primarily serves domestic and regional carriers connecting Colón with Panama City and other destinations within Panama.

Q: How far is the airport from Colón city center?
A: The airport is located on the outskirts of Colón, typically a short drive from the city center.

Q: Is the airport near the Panama Canal?
A: Yes, Colón sits near the Atlantic (Caribbean) entrance to the Panama Canal, making the airport convenient for visitors heading to canal-related attractions.

Q: Does the airport offer international flights?
A: Most scheduled commercial flights are domestic, with limited regional connectivity; Tocumen International Airport in Panama City handles the majority of international traffic.
transport_tips: Taxis are readily available outside the terminal and are the most common way to reach Colón city center or the Colón Free Zone. Rental car services can be arranged but advance booking is recommended. Travelers heading onward to Panama City can connect via domestic flight to Tocumen or Marcos A. Gelabert Airport rather than driving the approximately 80 km route.
local_tip: If visiting the Colón Free Zone, ask your hotel or a local contact to recommend a registered shopping transport service—these often include smoother customs processing and better negotiated rates than ad-hoc taxis.
